rationale: The two solutions share the same data tables and the same Verses and Song functions, so the difference lies in Verse. B wraps the whole cumulative section in one clear guard (v > 1 && v < len(creatures)) and then runs a plain countdown loop. It builds each line once and appends the spider suffix only when the caught creature is the spider, so the sentence template is not duplicated. It reuses comments[0] for the closing fly line. A folds the guard into the loop condition (i > 1 && i < len(animals)) and repeats the same guard separately for the final line. It hard-codes the whole spider sentence in a special branch keyed to i == 3 and repeats the fly line as a literal. Both are readable, but B has less duplication and its control flow is clearer.
